title: Arabic script — ICAO Doc 9303 Part 3 recommended MRZ transliteration
authority: ICAO Doc 9303 Machine Readable Travel Documents, Part 3, Section 6 Table C and Appendix B (7th ed. 2015; 8th ed. 2021)
description: Letter-for-letter, Buckwalter-based transliteration of Arabic-script names for the machine-readable zone, recommended by ICAO for search and matching. Letters without a plain Latin equivalent get an X escape (XKH, XTH, XSH, XH = ح); vowel marks are not encoded, shadda doubles the code, ة is XTA or XAH at the end of a name component. Covers the Persian, Urdu and Pashto letters of Table C.
notes: Few issuing states use this table; most print phonetic spellings (ABU<BAKR<MOHAMMED) in both VIZ and MRZ. It is useful as a lossless, stable matching key.
Output keeps spaces between name components; converting to MRZ filler characters (<, <<) is a separate step.
The name lexicon is disabled: the written letters are transliterated as they are, without vocalisation (ICAO App. B.1: vowels are not represented).
Sun-letter assimilation is not reflected; a shadda written on the sun letter after the article is ignored (ALRAZY, not ALRRAZY). Other shaddas double the code (عبّاس EBBAS).
ڜ ڢ ڧ ڨ are 'not encoded' in Table C and are dropped (fallback: drop).
App. B.5.5 says Farsi yeh could be Y or XAY, but Table C gives XYA, which is used here.
The interscript map icao-fas-Arab-Latn-9303 disagrees with the ICAO text (ة → P, harakat produce output); it was not used.
